**Method.** I used the dry discharge rates from the playbook. Each approach's capacity is lanes × flow per lane: N 4980, E 4680, S 3195 and W 3000 vehicles per hour. The listed arrivals are hourly rates, so y = rate ÷ capacity. Lost time is 16 s per cycle, so total green = C − 16 s. I started from the Webster cycle C = 29/(1 − Y). I then added margin where demand is rising, so no backlog carries forward. S is padded slightly because it is the bottleneck.

| Window | Sum of y (Y) | Cycle used | Greens (N/E/S/W) | Capacity ÷ demand |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8:30 | 0.64 | 95 s | 12/21/33/13 | about 1.3 |
| 8:45 | 0.75 | 127 s | 16/29/48/18 | about 1.16 |
| 9:00 (peak) | 0.83 | 180 s | 26/44/65/29 | 1.09–1.11 for every approach |
| 9:15 | 0.68 | 100 s | 13/22/35/14 | about 1.2 |

- **Peak window.** The Webster cycle is 168 s. I lengthened it to 180 s so S could be padded without pushing N or W below about 1.05× demand. All four approaches then keep about 1.1× capacity.
- **Last window.** The cycle is slightly longer than Webster, which would be about 91 s. This clears any leftover queue so few vehicles are still queued at 9:30.
- **Gridlock.** No approach should build a large queue. All greens are within the 7–150 s limits.

I sized each window with the Webster method from the playbook. Arrivals are hourly rates, so y = rate ÷ (lanes × dry flow per lane). The dry flows are N 4980, E 4680, S 3195 and W 3000 vehicles per hour. Lost time is 16 s per cycle, so total green = C − 16.

| Window | Y | Cycle C | Total green | Notes |

| 1:30 | 0.72 | about 120 s | 104 s | Demand is rising, so the cycle is about 15 s above Webster's 104 s. |
| 1:45 | 0.83 | about 170 s | 154 s | This is the peak, so it gets the longest cycle. |
| 2:00 | 0.72 | about 108 s | 92 s | Demand is falling, so the cycle is back near Webster. |
| 2:15 | 0.61 | about 85 s | 69 s | Webster gives 74 s, but a cycle that short wastes too much on lost time. |

- **Split:** I split green by y, not by arrivals. S has the highest y, so it gets the largest green, about 39% of the total.
- **Capacity check:** Each approach discharges about 1.05 to 1.2 times its arrivals in every window, so no backlog should build up. In the peak window the tightest is W, at about 1.05 times its arrivals.
- **Limits:** All greens are inside the 7–150 s limit. Queues should stay far below the 40-per-lane gridlock threshold.

**Method:** I used the playbook's measured dry discharge rates. E has only 2 lanes because of the closure, so its capacity is about 3120 vehicles per hour. Storage is 40 vehicles per lane, which is 80 for E and W and 120 for N and S. I set each approach's y as its hourly arrival rate divided by (lanes × flow per lane). The arrival numbers are hourly rates, so there is no ×4.

| window | y (N / E / S / W) | Y | Webster C | cycle used | total green (C−16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8:30 | 0.102 / 0.218 / 0.225 / 0.113 | 0.66 | 85 s | 95 s | 79 s |
| 8:45 | 0.120 / 0.256 / 0.266 / 0.133 | 0.78 | 129 s | 140 s | 124 s |
| 9:00 | 0.131 / 0.276 / 0.288 / 0.143 | 0.84 | 179 s | 200 s | 184 s |
| 9:15 | 0.108 / 0.231 / 0.238 / 0.120 | 0.70 | 96 s | 100 s | 84 s |

- **Rising windows:** I added margin to the cycle in the first three windows so no backlog starts. 9:00 is the peak and gets the longest cycle.
- **Green split:** I split green by y share and padded S by about 10%, since it is the bottleneck.
- **Capacity check:** Every approach discharges at least 1.03× its arrivals in every window.
  - The tightest approaches are N at 8:30 (1.03×) and W at 9:00 (1.05×).
  - S has about 1.15–1.2× at 8:45 and 9:00, and more at the other times.
- **Gridlock:** I expect queues to stay well below the 80-vehicle limit on E and W, so there should be no gridlock.
- **Last window:** At 9:15, Y falls to 0.70, so I cut the cycle to 100 s to clear any leftover queue.
